messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test `testOptionGroupLong()` attempts to select an option from an OptionGroup where the options only have long names (no short option character). It creates an OptionGroup, adds two options with only long names "foo" and "bar", adds the group to Options, and parses the command line with "--bar". The test expects the group to have selected the "bar" option.

The current bug report states that if the selected option has no short name (opt field is null), calling `group.setSelected(option)` has no effect.

Looking at the `OptionGroup.setSelected(Option)` method, it sets the `selected` field, which is a String identifier, based on the `option.getOpt()` value. The method:
- Checks if option is null, if so resets selection.
- Otherwise, if no option was selected or the same option is selected again (compares to `selected.equals(option.getOpt())`), sets `selected = option.getOpt()`.
- Otherwise, it throws an exception.

The problem here is that the method uses `option.getOpt()` as the key for selection, but from `Option.getOpt()`, the `opt` field is the short name (single character), and it may be null if the option only has a long name.

From `Option.getKey()`, we see the key to identify an option is:
- if `opt` (short name) is null, then the longOpt string is the key.
- otherwise, the short opt is the key.

Now in `OptionGroup.addOption(Option)`, the option is stored in a map keyed by `getKey()`, which returns either the short name or the long name if short name is null. This means the map keys correctly handle options with only long names.

However, `setSelected(Option)` relies on `option.getOpt()` which is the short name and can be null. If null, then the selected field remains null or unchanged, and thus the group does not recognize the selected option that only has a long name.

Finally, in `testOptionGroupLong()`, the options only have long names without short names, so `option.getOpt()` returns null. Thus, `setSelected()` fails to update the selected option.

Hence, the root cause is that `OptionGroup.setSelected(Option)` uses `option.getOpt()` (short name) to identify the option when selecting it, whereas it should use `option.getKey()` which properly returns the identifier whether it is a short or long name. Using `option.getKey()` would correctly identify options without short names.

This mismatch causes options with only a long name to never be recognized as selected in the OptionGroup. This is why the test fails and why the issue reports "OptionGroup doesn't play nice with options with a long name and no short name".

No other recent issues are directly relevant here.

Summary: The bug arises because OptionGroup.setSelected incorrectly uses option.getOpt() (short option) to identify the option, but for options with no short name (opt = null), it should use option.getKey() which falls back to the long option string. This causes setSelected to ignore options with only long names.

Suggested fix: Change OptionGroup.setSelected to use option.getKey() instead of option.getOpt() for consistent identification.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
